I am a 58-year-old farmer in Mtwara, and this 0.43-hectare plot is under cashew trees that have been here for many years. I do not buy chemical fertilizer for this plot because the cost is too high for a smallholder like me, and the sandy soils here do not respond well to small amounts anyway. I will spray pesticide when the nuts are forming to keep the insects away, as cashew is my main cash crop and I cannot afford to lose the harvest. My family will do the weeding and harvesting, and I may hire a few young men from the village for a short time during the busy harvest period.
